## Hands-on 2 – The menu {#hands-on-2-the-menu .smaller}

::: {.small}
**Task 4 is exploratory.** `try_spec()` with no arguments is the reproduced specification, the model of C6HJR, and every argument defaults to it. Run it and read *b*, the claim-aligned partial *r*, the CR2 p and the placement among the `r format(nrow(spec_curve), big.mark = ",")`, the lines that every try prints.
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# The reproduced specification, the model of C6HJR in Task 3
try_spec()
```

::: notes
Task 4 is exploration. The cell calls `try_spec()` with no arguments, which gives the reproduced specification, my own model, since every argument defaults to it. Run it and read the printout: the slope with its conventional t, the claim-aligned partial r, the CR2 p-value, the class and the placement among the eight hundred and sixty-four, the same lines that every try prints. Nothing is fitted here, because the result is read from the curve that the slides loaded with the data, and the IDE workspace fits the same model and returns the same numbers. [run it on the projector, then advance]
:::

## Hands-on 2 – One decision at a time {#hands-on-2-one-decision-at-a-time .smaller .output-8}

::: {.small}
Change **one decision** and hold the others; then edit either cell for a decision of your own, `outcome = "mpos"`, `noop = "drop"` or `measure = "es_2064_pop"`, or one off the curve, `estimator = "pooled_cl"`, to read why it is refused.
:::

::: {.fs-80}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
try_spec(estimator = "fe_country")  # country effects only: changes common to all of Europe stay in
```
:::

::: {.fs-80}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
try_spec(predictor = "growth")  # GDP growth instead of unemployment, in the World Bank series
```
:::

::: notes
The first cell keeps the country effects and drops the year effects, which is a change of estimator, and the second measures the economy by GDP growth, a change of predictor, with the sign reversed so that below zero stays the direction of the claim. Run both and read what moved. Then edit either cell for a decision of your own, three or four tries in all, and ask for one option off the curve as well, so that you read the reason that comes back and the page of the workshop's website that teaches it. [circulate; keep the Class results page on the other screen]
:::

## Hands-on 2 – The submission {#hands-on-2-the-submission .smaller .output-8}

::: {.small}
`my_experiments()` lists every try side by side. Rerun the one that you would defend and **submit it**: the cell prints your tag, such as `amber-otter-42`, and a link to the form, and your dot joins the class chart of the [Class results]({{< var live-results-url >}}) page.
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
my_experiments()
```

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
submit_exploration()
```

::: notes
When you have three or four tries, print the log. `my_experiments()` lists the tries side by side, showing only the decisions that you varied, which makes up the small multiverse that you have just built. Then rerun the try for which you can argue best, so that it is your last, and submit it. The cell prints your submission line, a link to a form with every field filled in, and a tag that marks your dot on the class chart. Press Send in the form, and the dot appears on the Class results page within seconds, labelled exploratory because you chose it after looking at the results. [wait for the dots; then read the chart]
:::
